The object is 赤いズボン ("red pants"), with the i-adjective 赤い qualifying ズボン, marked by を as the direct object. The verb はく ("to wear/put on", for clothing on the lower body) appears in the continuous past (はいて + いた): the て form + いる indicates a state/continuous action, and いた is in the past, giving "was wearing". The target is coverage, practicing a color adjective + a verb in the continuous past aspect ています/ていた.

structure_explanation.en: The sentence has the topic 彼は (he), the object 職務を (the duty/assignment) marked by を, and the verb 与える (to give) in the passive voice: 与え + られ (passive) + た (past). The construction ～られた indicates that something was done to the subject, i.e. he was the target of the act of giving. In Portuguese it is more natural to translate as 'received', because the Japanese passive with verbs of giving usually corresponds to our 'to receive'.

A construção ～られた indica que algo foi feito ao sujeito, ou seja, ele foi alvo da ação de dar. Em pt-BR fica mais natural traduzir como 'recebeu', porque a passiva japonesa com verbos de dar costuma equivaler ao nosso 'receber'.
